title: SSL & DNS cutover
intro: Point your domains at Tugra, host by host. Certificates are issued fresh on Tugra and are not assumed to carry over from the source. When a DNS-01 certificate can be issued ahead of time, TLS is valid on the very first request after the flip; otherwise there is a bounded window until the certificate is issued once DNS points here. Cloudflare-managed hosts are flipped for you; for any other DNS provider you get the exact records to copy.

probe.label: Probe from
probe.agentNote: Probing from the target server checks that the app is reachable from where it runs; a hub probe checks what the public internet sees.

seed.title: Apply staged certificates
seed.body: Staged certificates from the migration are applied to the server's proxy, which restarts for a few seconds and briefly drops ingress for every app on that server. Continue?

flip.title: Plan and flip DNS
flip.honest: TLS is valid on the first request only for hosts whose certificate is already issued (DNS-01 pre-issue). For other hosts there is a bounded window between the DNS change and certificate issuance, and some clients keep resolving the old address until the TTL expires.
flip.summary: {count} host(s) will change; estimated {minutes} min at the current batch settings.
flip.stopOnFail: Stop the run when a host fails verification
flip.keepProxied: Keep Cloudflare proxying on hosts that already have it
flip.autoRevert: Automatically revert a host that fails verification
flip.autoRevertWarn: Off by default. Auto-revert is never applied to stateful apps, because a revert cannot restore data written on Tugra.
flip.skipTtlWait: Do not wait for the old TTL to expire before flipping
flip.acceptDataRisk: I understand that some of these apps hold state: until the source app is stopped, clients with the old DNS keep writing to the source, so the two copies can diverge.
flip.acceptHttp01Gap: I understand that some hosts have no certificate yet, so HTTPS may fail for a short window after the flip until it is issued.
flip.noteStaleTtl: Clients keep the old address until its TTL expires, so lower the TTL first and wait.
flip.noteProxiedTtl: Proxied Cloudflare records ignore the TTL; propagation depends on the proxy.

revert.title: Revert DNS
revert.hosts: DNS will be restored to its pre-flip records for {count} host(s):
revert.dataLoss: Revert restores the DNS records exactly, but it cannot restore data written on Tugra after the flip. Anything created there since the flip stays behind.
revert.ackDataLoss: I understand that data written on Tugra after the flip is not restored.
revert.force: Force the revert even if the records changed since the flip

sourceStop.title: Stop the source app
sourceStop.body: The migration token for the source is read-only, so Tugra never stops the source for you. After a flip, stop each source app yourself:
sourceStop.staleDns: Until it is stopped, clients that still resolve the old DNS keep reaching the source app.
sourceStop.splitBrain: Some of these apps hold state: while both copies run, writes can land on either one and diverge (split brain). Stop the source as soon as the flip is verified.

warn.staleAaaa: A stale IPv6 (AAAA) record is deleted
warn.wildcardExplicitRecord: An explicit record is added next to a wildcard record
warn.ttlNotWaited: The old TTL has not expired yet
warn.gapHttp01: No certificate yet: HTTPS can fail briefly until HTTP-01 issues it
warn.stateful: Stateful app: the source and Tugra can diverge until the source is stopped
warn.caa: A CAA record may restrict certificate issuance
warn.coverageUnverified: DNS credential coverage of this zone is unverified
warn.sslModeWeak: Cloudflare SSL mode is weak for an origin certificate
warn.sslModeUnknown: Cloudflare SSL mode could not be read
warn.sslModeBad: Cloudflare SSL mode will break HTTPS to the origin
warn.staleTtl: Resolvers keep the old record until its TTL expires
warn.quiesceSource: Stop writes on the source before flipping stateful apps
warn.tokenCopied: This server holds a copy of a team DNS token; rotating the credential does not update it until you re-apply it
